name: The diaTribe Foundation
why_relevant: Diabetes journalism with a research-literate readership; already a direct-fit org in diabetes-orgs-catalogue
suggested_ask: Pitch a short explainer on why no published human baseline for CGM prediction exists

name: The Diabetes Link
why_relevant: Serves young adults with diabetes at university age - the study recruits adults 18+, and this is the cleanest 18-25 channel found
suggested_ask: Ask about a campus-chapter share of the study; they have an existing student network

name: Diabetes Technology Society (DTS)
why_relevant: Runs the standards and meetings where CGM accuracy and algorithms are argued about. Benchmark credibility lives here
suggested_ask: Ask about an abstract or poster slot; ATTD/DTS-style venues suit a human-baseline result

name: Diabetes Center Berne
why_relevant: Swiss diabetes-technology research centre that funds and hosts digital-diabetes projects; EU-adjacent and reachable from Rostock
suggested_ask: Ask about a research collaboration or their innovation programme

name: Glooko
why_relevant: CGM and pump data-platform company. Their whole product is the data Sugar-Sugar plays back
suggested_ask: Data-partnership or co-marketing conversation, not a recruitment post

name: ECSA - European Citizen Science Association
why_relevant: Sugar-Sugar is a citizen-science study with ethics approval and open code - exactly what ECSA amplifies, and it is European
suggested_ask: Ask to be listed in their project directory and newsletter
notes: Verified on LinkedIn 2026-08-27. Strongest non-diabetes fit found

name: American Association of Clinical Endocrinology (AACE)
why_relevant: Clinician body. Reaches the endocrinologists who would have to trust a prediction model
suggested_ask: Protocol-and-ethics framing; conference or newsletter mention

name: Diabetesliitto (Finnish Diabetes Association)

suggested_ask: Ask about a member-newsletter mention of the study

name: Bigfoot Biomedical
